I need the front end for Patchbay. A free, volunteer-maintained show-building tool a low-power community FM station uses so its volunteer hosts can assemble each broadcast hour from music, voice segments, PSAs and required announcements.

Who's using it: Walt Henderson, 58, a postal carrier who has hosted 'Back Porch Blues' every Thursday 8–10pm on WCRV 99.1, a volunteer-run low-power station in a small Kentucky town, for seven years. He knows his music deeply, but he's not a sound engineer, and he prepares his show at home on Wednesday nights.

What they're doing right now: He's putting together Thursday's two-hour show, a tribute to Memphis Minnie with a recorded 9-minute interview he did with a local guitarist. He's arranging the pieces in order: his recorded intro, 24 tracks, the interview split into two parts with a song between them, and two underwriting spots for the hardware store and the diner, which the station promised to air. He also needs a community calendar PSA and the legal station ID that must fall near the top of each hour. The first hour currently runs 4 minutes long, which pushes the 9pm ID late. He has to trim or swap a track, cut a long pause out of the interview, and put a quick fade between two songs before he submits the show for Thursday.

What's in the system at this point: Station music library of 3,812 tracks, each with artist, title, year, duration, and a clean or explicit flag. Walt's prepared items: intro voice track (1:12), 24 selected tracks from 2:18 to 6:40 long, interview audio in two parts (5:02 and 4:21, with a 7-second silence at 3:40 in part 1), 2 underwriting spots (Hensley Hardware 0:30, Rosie's Diner 0:30, each due once per hour), community calendar PSA (1:00), and the legal ID (0:10, required between 8:58 and 9:02 and between 9:58 and 10:02). Hour 1 adds up to 64:03. The show slot is Thursday 26 Nov 2026, 8:00–10:00pm. His previous 12 shows are saved as templates.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
